evidence.snippet: (ii) hepatomyocerebral: in case of liver, brain and muscle involvement (weakness/fatigue, ptosis, ophthalmoplegia, myalgia, dysphonia, dysphagia)
evidence.explanation: Muscle signs are the defining addition in the hepatomyocerebral subgroup.

steps/31.description: Weakness or fatigue is one of the muscle features that define the hepatomyocerebral subtype. The 20.8% cohort figure is for all 159 patients with data and includes the adult isolated-myopathy cases, which are outside this entry, so no frequency is given.

evidence.snippet: Weakness or fatigue was reported in 33/159 patients (20.8%), ptosis in 22/159 (13.8%), progressive external ophthalmoplegia in 14/159 (8.8%), myalgia in 12/159 (7.5%), dysphagia in 12/159 (7.5%) and dysphonia in 8/159 (5.0%).
evidence.explanation: Frequency of ptosis across the whole cohort, including adult-onset cases.

evidence.snippet: (ii) hepatomyocerebral: in case of liver, brain and muscle involvement (weakness/fatigue, ptosis, ophthalmoplegia, myalgia, dysphonia, dysphagia)
evidence.explanation: Ptosis is one of the defining muscle signs of the hepatomyocerebral subgroup.

steps/32.description: Ptosis is another defining muscle feature of the hepatomyocerebral subtype. The 13.8% cohort figure includes the adult isolated-myopathy cases, so no frequency is given.

evidence.snippet: The main supply of deoxyribonucleotides (dNTPs) for mtDNA synthesis comes from the salvage pathway initiated by dGK and thymidine kinase-2 (TK2).
evidence.explanation: Places dGK at the start of the salvage pathway supplying mtDNA precursors.

edges/1.description: Without dGK, the mitochondrial salvage phosphorylation of deoxyguanosine and deoxyadenosine, the first and rate-limiting step, does not occur.

edges/2.description: The same precursor shortage limits mtDNA replication in skeletal muscle, less consistently than in liver.

evidence.snippet: Autosomal recessive pathogenetic variants in the DGUOK gene cause a lack of dGk enzyme activity and consequently unbalanced dNTP pool for the reduction of deoxy purines versus deoxy pyrimidines, ultimately leading to mtDNA depletion and/or multiple deletions.
evidence.explanation: States the chain from enzyme loss through dNTP imbalance to mtDNA depletion; an introduction sentence, not a result of the cohort study.

evidence.snippet: The association of mtDNA depletion with mutated DGUOK suggests that the salvage-pathway enzymes are involved in the maintenance of balanced mitochondrial dNTP pools.
evidence.explanation: The discovery paper's inference linking dGK loss to dNTP pool balance and mtDNA depletion.

edges/3.description: Insufficient purine precursors limit mtDNA replication, lowering mtDNA copy number.

evidence.snippet: Defective mtDNA leads to organ dysfunction due to insufficient mtDNA-encoded protein synthesis, resulting in an inadequate energy production to meet the needs of affected organs.
evidence.explanation: Review synthesis of the depletion-to-energy-failure link across mtDNA maintenance defects.

evidence.snippet: The mtDNA-encoded protein cytochrome c oxidase was much lower in Dguok-/- liver tissue than in the wt, whereas the expression of the nuclear-encoded succinate dehydrogenase complex subunit A was unaffected.
evidence.explanation: In the knockout liver the mtDNA-encoded subunit falls while the nuclear-encoded one is preserved, the signature of depletion-driven deficiency.

edges/4.description: Fewer mtDNA templates mean less synthesis of the 13 mtDNA-encoded respiratory chain subunits, with the entirely nuclear-encoded complex II spared.

evidence.snippet: Defective mtDNA leads to organ dysfunction due to insufficient mtDNA-encoded protein synthesis, resulting in an inadequate energy production to meet the needs of affected organs.
evidence.explanation: Review synthesis linking the respiratory chain defect to organ dysfunction.

edges/5.description: Energy failure in hepatocytes drives cholestasis, steatosis, fibrosis and necrosis and, in most infants, liver failure.

evidence.snippet: DGUOK mutant iHep and iHep-Orgs, but not control and corrected one, are more sensitive to iron overload-induced ferroptosis, which can be rescued by N-Acetylcysteine (NAC).
evidence.explanation: Patient iPSC-derived hepatocytes and organoids, with CRISPR-corrected isogenic controls, show DGUOK-dependent ferroptosis sensitivity.

edges/6.description: DGUOK-mutant hepatocytes are more susceptible to iron-induced ferroptosis than isogenic corrected cells; shown in vitro only.

evidence.snippet: Defective mtDNA leads to organ dysfunction due to insufficient mtDNA-encoded protein synthesis, resulting in an inadequate energy production to meet the needs of affected organs.
evidence.explanation: General review statement; it is not specific to brain in DGUOK deficiency.

edges/7.description: The same energy failure is the presumed cause of the neurological signs. The sources cited here do not document brain mtDNA depletion or brain respiratory chain activity, and a contribution from liver failure itself cannot be excluded; see the discussion on this node.

evidence.snippet: For metabolites, we analyzed lactate/pyruvate ratio and observed a significant increase in patient iHep compared to control and corrected iHep (Figure 3L).
evidence.explanation: A raised lactate/pyruvate ratio in DGUOK-mutant iPSC hepatocytes that normalises in the CRISPR-corrected isogenic line ties the lactate shift to the DGUOK defect; shown in vitro, not in patient tissue.

evidence.snippet: Brain MRS analysis showed a lactate peak in 6/8 patients.
evidence.explanation: Lactate accumulation in brain tissue of patients, consistent with local oxidative failure; supports the edge indirectly because it shows lactate rising in an affected tissue rather than proving the mechanism.

edges/8.description: Impaired oxidative phosphorylation shifts pyruvate to lactate. Lactate may be only mildly raised early in the course.

edges/9.description: Lactate accumulation is the presumed main contributor. The cohort does not break metabolic acidosis down by cause, and liver failure and renal involvement may also contribute, so this edge is an inference.

edges/10.description: Ferroptotic hepatocyte death is proposed to contribute to liver damage.

edges/20.description: Raised plasma tyrosine is a marker of hepatocellular dysfunction here; it is detected on newborn screening in some infants.

evidence.snippet: In our patient, levels were as high as 29,090 ng/mL, which may occur due to the liver regeneration process or the early onset of hepatocellular carcinoma.
evidence.explanation: The authors' two candidate explanations for the AFP elevation; neither is established.

edges/21.description: Very high AFP accompanies the liver disease; regeneration and early carcinoma have both been proposed as its source.

evidence.snippet: One of our patients underwent liver transplantation; pathologic findings revealed (in addition to diffuse hepatopathy) a hepatocellular carcinoma, implying a possible link between mtDNA depletion syndrome and tumorigenesis.
evidence.explanation: Case-level observation and the authors' proposed link.

edges/22.description: Hepatocellular carcinoma has been found in infants with DGUOK deficiency, as early as six months of age, including incidentally in an explant. The link between mtDNA depletion and tumorigenesis is proposed by the reporting authors, not demonstrated; whether it runs through cirrhosis and regeneration or through a cell-autonomous effect of mitochondrial dysfunction is unknown.

edges/23.description: Impaired hepatic glucose production in the failing liver is the presumed contribution. This edge is an inference from the liver disease; no cited source isolates the hepatic contribution from the islet-cell one.

evidence.snippet: islet cell hyperplasia (and hyperinsulinism) may contribute to MDS-associated hypoglycemia
evidence.explanation: The authors' hypothesis from autopsy findings.

evidence.snippet: In both patients, critical samples demonstrated hypoketotic hypoglycemia and a partial glycemic response to glucagon stimulation, thereby suggesting hyperinsulinism (HI).
evidence.explanation: Biochemical evidence of hyperinsulinism in two further infants.

edges/24.description: Inappropriate insulin secretion may contribute to hypoketotic hypoglycaemia.

evidence.snippet: DGUOK | HGNC:2858 | mitochondrial disease | MONDO:0044970 | AR | Definitive
evidence.explanation: ClinGen gene-disease validity row.

evidence.snippet: We identified a single-nucleotide deletion (204delA) within the coding region of DGUOK that segregates with the disease in the three kindreds studied.
evidence.explanation: Original gene discovery by homozygosity mapping in Druze kindreds.

evidence.snippet: DGUOK | deoxyguanosine kinase | hgnc:2858 | Disease-causing germline mutation(s) in
evidence.explanation: Orphanet gene-disease row.

genes/0.notes: ClinGen classifies DGUOK with Definitive validity, but for a lumped "mitochondrial disease" (MONDO:0044970) covering this entry, noncirrhotic portal hypertension 1 and adult-onset PEO/myopathy with multiple mtDNA deletions. Truncating, splice, missense and intragenic-deletion alleles are all reported.

evidence.snippet: Liver transplant significantly modified the survival rate in 26 treated patients when compared with untreated.
evidence.explanation: Survival benefit in the largest cohort (retrospective, not randomised).

evidence.snippet: However, patients with nystagmus at disease onset had a negative outcome after LTx with a statistically significant difference in survival rate (Kaplan-Meier, P = 0.0275) (Fig. 3C).
evidence.explanation: Nystagmus at onset predicts worse post-transplant survival.

evidence.snippet: Liver transplantation has been used to treat individuals without neurologic involvement or with minimal neurologic involvement.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews selection criterion.

evidence.snippet: In the presence of these features, there is increased mortality, and liver transplantation does not confer increased survival.
evidence.explanation: Refutes benefit in children with profound hypotonia, significant psychomotor retardation or nystagmus.

evidence.snippet: The 1-year survival rate was 64%; 36% survived for more than 5 years.
evidence.explanation: Post-transplant survival in 14 children.

evidence.snippet: Twenty-three patients received liver transplants, of whom 12 died within 2 years of transplant.
evidence.explanation: High early post-transplant mortality in an independent collation.

evidence.snippet: Causes of death in transplanted patients were pulmonary hypertension in 4/13 (30.8%), LTx complications in 2/13 (15.4%)
evidence.explanation: Pulmonary hypertension led the causes of post-transplant death.

treatments/0.description: The only intervention shown to change survival, and a contested one. The 2024 international cohort found transplantation significantly improved survival in 26 patients and, unlike earlier analyses, found no survival difference by presence of neurological involvement overall, though nystagmus at onset predicted worse post-transplant survival. A 2008 review concluded that profound hypotonia, psychomotor retardation or nystagmus make transplantation futile; GeneReviews limits it to children without, or with minimal, neurological involvement. About half of transplanted children in a separate collation died within two years, and neurological or muscle disease can emerge afterwards. Pulmonary hypertension was the most frequent cause of death after transplantation in the 2024 cohort (4 of 13 post-transplant deaths), which is relevant to post-transplant follow-up.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Replaces the depleted, failing liver; does not correct extrahepatic tissues.

evidence.snippet: Children with cholestatic liver disease may require formulas with enriched medium-chain triglyceride content and fractional meals with enteral nutrition at night for adequate nutrition.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews nutritional management.

treatments/1.description: MCT-enriched formula, fractional daytime meals with overnight enteral feeding, fat-soluble vitamin and essential fatty acid supplementation, and feeding therapy or gastrostomy as needed.

evidence.snippet: Cornstarch for those with symptomatic hypoglycemia; supplementation with fat-soluble vitamins and essential fatty acids
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews recommendation.

treatments/2.description: Cornstarch for symptomatic hypoglycaemia, with fasting glucose monitored during infancy.

evidence.snippet: routine immunizations for affected individuals and household contacts to prevent viral illness
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews recommendation.

treatments/3.description: Routine immunisation of the child and household contacts to reduce viral illness.

evidence.snippet: However, in adult dguok-/- fish we detected a significant increase in liver mtDNA copy number when supplemented with both purine nucleosides.
evidence.explanation: Liver mtDNA rescue in adult mutant fish with both purine nucleosides.

evidence.snippet: When supplemented with only one purine nucleoside (dGuo), mtDNA copy number in both mutant and wt juvenile animals was significantly reduced, contrasting with previous cell culture studies, possibly because of nucleotide pool imbalance.
evidence.explanation: Single-nucleoside supplementation lowered mtDNA in juveniles, a caution against deoxyguanosine alone.

evidence.snippet: CERC-913 increased mtDNA content in DGUOK-deficient hepatocytes up to 2.4-fold after 4 days of treatment in a dose-dependent fashion, which was significantly more effective than dGMP at similar concentrations.
evidence.explanation: Prodrug rescue in cultured knockout rat hepatocytes.

treatments/4.description: Substrate enhancement to bypass the missing kinase: purine deoxynucleosides or a dGMP prodrug (CERC-913). Evidence is preclinical only (zebrafish, rat hepatocyte cultures); no human treatment data for DGUOK deficiency are cited here and no DGUOK trial was found on ClinicalTrials.gov.

treatments/4/targets/0.description: Increases substrate for, or bypasses, the missing phosphorylation step.

evidence.snippet: Carrier testing for at-risk relatives, prenatal testing for a pregnancy at increased risk, and preimplantation genetic testing are possible if the DGUOK pathogenic variants in the family are known.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews counselling statement.

evidence.snippet: At conception, each sib of an affected individual has a 25% chance of being affected, a 50% chance of being an asymptomatic carrier, and a 25% chance of being unaffected and not a carrier.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews statement of the sibling recurrence risk.

treatments/5.description: Autosomal recessive recurrence risk of 25%; carrier testing, prenatal testing and preimplantation genetic testing are available once the familial variants are known.

evidence.snippet: Long-term survival is best predicted by the absence of profound hypotonia, significant psychomotor retardation, or nystagmus.
evidence.explanation: The restrictive position.

evidence.snippet: We compared the survival rate of individuals with or without neurological involvement but there was no statistically significant difference (Kaplan-Meier, P = 0.5410) (Fig. 3B).
evidence.explanation: The later cohort finding that neurological involvement as a whole did not predict post-transplant survival.

evidence.snippet: Nevertheless, a decision to carry out LT for patients with DGUOK deficiency remains difficult because neurological symptoms may occur and worsen after LT despite their absence before transplantation.
evidence.explanation: Neurological outcome after transplantation is not predictable from pre-transplant status.

open_questions/0.rationale: A 2008 systematic review found that profound hypotonia, significant psychomotor retardation or nystagmus predicted death and that transplantation did not improve survival when they were present. The 2024 international cohort (26 transplanted) found no survival difference by neurological involvement, MRI abnormality, hypotonia or psychomotor delay, but did find worse survival with nystagmus at onset. A single-centre series reported long-term survivors with mild pre-transplant neurological signs. All data are retrospective and subject to selection, so the question is open; nystagmus is the sign on which the studies agree.

evidence.snippet: No genotype-phenotype correlation was identified.
evidence.explanation: The negative finding.

evidence.snippet: Patients with two truncating variants had a higher risk of death and were more likely to have the neonatal/infantile-onset hepatocerebral disease phenotype.
evidence.explanation: The positive finding.

evidence.snippet: All patients who harbor null mutations had early onset liver failure and significant neurological disease.
evidence.explanation: Earlier series consistent with a null-allele effect.

open_questions/1.rationale: Two overlapping 2024 literature cohorts disagree. One reports no genotype-phenotype correlation; the other finds that two truncating alleles raise the risk of death and of the hepatocerebral phenotype. The 2008 series had already noted that every patient with two null alleles had early liver failure and neurological disease. The difference may reflect how variants were grouped rather than contradictory data, but it bears on prognostic counselling after a molecular diagnosis.

evidence.snippet: Only six patients had additional mild neurological signs after liver transplant.
evidence.explanation: New neurological signs after transplantation.

open_questions/2.rationale: The sources cited here document mtDNA depletion in liver, muscle and blood but not in brain, and the knockout mouse has no neurological phenotype. Neurological signs can appear after liver transplantation, which argues for a primary CNS component, but that observation does not measure brain mtDNA. The answer matters for transplant selection and for whether a nucleoside therapy would need to reach the brain.

evidence.snippet: In our patient, levels were as high as 29,090 ng/mL, which may occur due to the liver regeneration process or the early onset of hepatocellular carcinoma.
evidence.explanation: AFP elevation is ambiguous between regeneration and tumour.

open_questions/3.rationale: HCC is documented in single patients from infancy, and GeneReviews recommends three-monthly AFP and ultrasound, but no cohort gives an incidence, and AFP is already very high from the liver disease, which limits it as a tumour marker. Evidence for the surveillance interval is expert opinion.

evidence.snippet: Since systemic mastocytosis often associates with the presence in hematopoietic cells of a somatic gain-of-function variant in KIT, D816V-KIT, we examined its potential role in IL-6 upregulation.
evidence.explanation: Establishes D816V-KIT as a somatic gain-of-function variant in haematopoietic cells. Graded INDIRECT because the framing is systemic mastocytosis rather than MMAS, and the shared driver is the point being relied on.

steps/1.description: An activating KIT variant, characteristically D816V, arises somatically in the mast cell lineage. The variant is the same one that drives systemic mastocytosis, and the distinguishing feature of this disorder is quantitative: the clone stays below the mast cell burden that the systemic mastocytosis criteria require. Nothing about the variant itself is different, which is why the entry does not claim a distinct molecular lesion.

evidence.snippet: We further demonstrate that aberrant KIT activity and signaling are critical for the induction of IL-6 and involve STAT5 and PI3K pathways but not STAT3 or STAT4.
evidence.explanation: Identifies the pathways carrying the constitutive signal, and excludes two others.

evidence.snippet: Activation of STAT5A and STAT5B downstream of D816V-KIT was mediated by JAK2 but also by MEK/ERK1/2, which not only promoted STAT5 phosphorylation but also its long-term transcription.
evidence.explanation: Details the kinases through which the constitutive signal reaches STAT5.

steps/2.description: D816V-KIT signals constitutively through STAT5 and PI3K, with STAT5A and STAT5B activation mediated by JAK2 and also by MEK and ERK1/2, the latter driving both STAT5 phosphorylation and its long-term transcription. STAT3 and STAT4 are not involved. The functional consequence demonstrated in this pathway is persistent IL-6 production by the mast cell itself, which links the clone to a systemic inflammatory output independent of degranulation.

evidence.snippet: There also may be unknown diseases of mast cell activation, in which mast cells either activate at a lower threshold of stimulation, or perhaps resist the usual stimuli to degranulate. The explanation for why some patients would have unexplained flushing or anaphylaxis would then be an abnormal sensitivity of their mast cells to activation
evidence.explanation: The consensus-conference formulation of the lowered-threshold hypothesis, quoted in a criteria paper. Graded INDIRECT and evidence_source OTHER because it is expert reasoning about a then-hypothetical disease class, not a measurement; it is curated because it is the origin of this node's claim rather than confirmation of it.

steps/3.description: The clonal mast cells activate and degranulate on stimuli that would not trigger normal mast cells, which is what converts a small clone into a systemic clinical syndrome. This is the node the entry is least able to source directly: the concept was articulated at the consensus conference that classified systemic mastocytosis variants, as a hypothesis, and the evidence curated here is that statement of the hypothesis rather than a measurement in MMAS patients. The `directness: INDIRECT` grading and this note are the honest description of its status.

evidence.snippet: In this article, we discuss diagnostic features and criteria and propose a ICD-10-CM-adjusted classification for disorders associated with MCA, herein referred to as MCA disorders (MCADs), with special emphasis on the delineation between confirmed MCAS, MCAD not fulfilling MCAS criteria, and suspected MCAD that is not present.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that the classification turns on which criteria are and are not fulfilled, which is the threshold logic this node encodes.

evidence.snippet: Flow cytometric analysis of bone marrow showed CD25 expression of MCs in all patients with SM and MMAS (range: 0.002-0.3% of cells).
evidence.explanation: The only direct measurement of the burden this node names, made in MMAS patients rather than in a neighbouring category: aberrant CD25-expressing mast cells are 0.002 to 0.3 per cent of bone marrow cells.

evidence.snippet: BMM patients were significantly older, predominantly male, had lower tryptase and lower burden of neoplastic mast cells, and displayed a higher frequency of allergic reactions, mainly triggered by Hymenoptera, than patients with typical ISM.
evidence.explanation: Describes an SM variant with low mast cell burden and hymenoptera-triggered reactions, which is the moving boundary this node sits against. Graded INDIRECT because the cohort is bone marrow mastocytosis, that is patients who do meet SM criteria.

steps/4.description: The clonal population does not reach the mast cell burden required by the systemic mastocytosis criteria. This node records the defining negative, and it is the reason the entry exists: the disorder is constituted by failing a threshold, so the negative is part of the mechanism rather than a caveat about it. It has no downstream edges by design. Note that where the threshold sits has moved - the 2021 refined bone marrow mastocytosis criteria describe an SM variant with lower neoplastic mast cell burden and more hymenoptera-triggered reactions than typical indolent systemic mastocytosis - so this node's extension depends on which criteria set is applied.

evidence.snippet: Although the release of mast cell (MC) mediators upon MC activation might present with a wide variety of symptoms, particular clinical features typically characterize MC mediator release episodes in patients with clonal MCD without skin involvement.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that mediator release episodes in clonal disease without skin involvement have a characteristic clinical shape, which is the claim this node makes.

evidence.snippet: When the symptoms are severe, systemic, and recurrent, and accompanied by a diagnostic increase in the serum tryptase level or other mast cell mediators, an MCA syndrome (MCAS) may be diagnosed.
evidence.explanation: States the severity, distribution, recurrence and mediator-rise pattern that defines the syndrome and that this node produces.

steps/5.description: Degranulation releases histamine, tryptase and other mediators, producing severe, recurrent, systemic symptoms across skin, gastrointestinal tract and cardiovascular system. In clonal disease the episodes have a characteristic shape - cardiovascular collapse predominating, frequently without urticaria - which is what makes hymenoptera anaphylaxis in a patient with no skin lesions the classic presentation.

evidence.snippet: The prevalence of anaphylaxis among patients with clonal mast cell disorders (MCD) is clearly higher comparing to the general population.
evidence.explanation: Establishes raised anaphylaxis prevalence in clonal mast cell disease, the group this entry belongs to.

evidence.snippet: Due to a lower frequency of symptoms outside of acute episodes, clonal MCD in the absence of skin lesions might sometimes be difficult to identify which may lead to underdiagnosis, and anaphylaxis is commonly the presenting symptom in these patients.
evidence.explanation: States that anaphylaxis is commonly the presenting symptom and that the disorder is underdiagnosed for lack of interval symptoms.

steps/6.description: Severe recurrent anaphylaxis, frequently hymenoptera-venom triggered and frequently without urticaria, and commonly the presenting event. Anaphylaxis prevalence in clonal mast cell disease is clearly higher than in the general population.

evidence.snippet: Although the release of mast cell (MC) mediators upon MC activation might present with a wide variety of symptoms, particular clinical features typically characterize MC mediator release episodes in patients with clonal MCD without skin involvement.
evidence.explanation: Supports a characteristic episode phenotype in clonal disease without skin involvement. Graded INDIRECT because the abstract does not itemise which features, so the specific attribution of hypotension rests on the anaphylaxis phenotype above.

steps/7.description: Hypotension during mediator release episodes, part of the cardiovascular-predominant episode pattern that characterises clonal disease without skin involvement.

evidence.snippet: Earlier proposed criteria for the diagnosis of MCAS included episodic symptoms consistent with mast cell mediator release affecting two or more organ systems with urticaria, angioedema, flushing, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal cramping, hypotensive syncope or near syncope, tachycardia, wheezing, conjunctival injection, pruritus, and nasal stuffiness.
evidence.explanation: Lists flushing among the episodic mediator-release symptoms in the diagnostic criteria.

evidence.snippet: Furthermore, mast cell lines expressing D816V-KIT, but not those expressing normal KIT or other KIT variants, produced constitutively high IL-6 amounts at the message and protein levels.
evidence.explanation: Shows the D816V variant specifically, and not normal KIT or other KIT variants, produces constitutive downstream output, which is the causal step this edge asserts.

evidence.snippet: Patients showing clonal BM MCs were grouped into indolent systemic mastocytosis without skin lesions (ISMs(-); n = 48) and other c-MCADs (n = 3)-both with CD25(++) BM MCs and either positive mast/stem cell growth factor receptor gene (KIT) mutation or clonal human androgen receptor assay (HUMARA) tests-and nc-MCAD (CD25-negative BM MCs in the absence of KIT mutation; n = 32) and compared for their clinical, biological, and molecular characteristics.
evidence.explanation: Defines the clonality criteria this entry rests on, and shows the clonal-but-not-SM group is small even within a referred cohort: three of eighty-three patients.

evidence.snippet: In bone marrow, the KIT D816V mutation was detected in all SM patients but in only 2 patients with MMAS (range: 0.007-9% mutated cells).
evidence.explanation: Graded REFUTE against treating KIT D816V as universal in this disorder: it was found in every systemic mastocytosis patient but in only two of four with MMAS, the rest being established as clonal on CD25 expression alone. evidence.snippet: Here, we review the relevant aspects related to the pathogenesis of MCAS, with special emphasis on the prevalence and diagnostic relevance of KIT mutations.

treatments/2.description: H1 and H2 histamine receptor antagonists, anti-leukotrienes and mast cell stabilisers such as cromolyn, used to suppress mediator production or block mediator effects between and during episodes. Response to these agents is not merely therapeutic: a decrease in frequency or severity of symptoms on anti-mediator therapy is itself one of the diagnostic criteria for the syndrome, so treatment and diagnosis are entangled here in a way they are not in most entries.

open_questions/0.rationale: This entity is defined by failing the systemic mastocytosis criteria, so redefining those criteria redefines it, without anybody restudying it. The 2021 refined criteria carve out bone marrow mastocytosis as an SM variant that is older, more male, has lower tryptase and lower neoplastic mast cell burden, and has more hymenoptera-triggered allergic reactions than typical indolent systemic mastocytosis. That is the same clinical description this category was assembled from, on the other side of the threshold. No study has reclassified an MMAS cohort under the refined criteria to see what is left, and the original cohort had three such patients, so the question is whether the category survives as a population or only as a residual definition. Until that is answered, no prevalence or frequency figure for this entry is stable.

open_questions/1.rationale: The lowered-threshold model is the link between a very small clone and a systemic clinical syndrome, and it is the load-bearing step in the mechanism. Its origin is a consensus-conference conjecture about a then-hypothetical class of disease, quoted in the 2010 criteria paper, and the sources curated here contain no measurement of activation threshold in patients with this diagnosis. The alternative account - that mediator output scales with clone size and the syndrome is simply the low end of systemic mastocytosis - is not excluded by anything cited, and would predict that MMAS and low-burden systemic mastocytosis are one continuum, which is what the boundary question above asks from the other direction.

open_questions/2.rationale: The 2010 criteria paper states in its own abstract that MCAS as a distinct clinical entity has not been generally accepted and that definitive diagnostic criteria do not exist, and it proposes criteria explicitly as a basis for further study and validation. The 2022 ECNM-AIM classification is a substantial advance but is itself framed as a proposal and notes that validated diagnostic criteria for implicating suspected mast cell activation are lacking. The monoclonal subset is the best-defined part of that landscape, because clonality is a demonstrable laboratory fact rather than a symptom pattern, which is why this entry curates it rather than the broader category. The contestedness is recorded because it bounds how much weight any epidemiology or phenotype frequency here can carry.

steps/1.description: KIF7, the human ortholog of Drosophila Costal2, is an immotile kinesin-4 protein that localizes to the tip of the primary cilium, where it regulates the GLI transcription factors of the Hedgehog pathway. In the absence of Hedgehog ligand KIF7 promotes processing of GLI3 into its transcriptional repressor form; biallelic loss-of-function KIF7 mutations deregulate most GLI target genes and impair GLI3 processing, disrupting the tightly dosed Hedgehog output required for skeletal, limb, and craniofacial patterning. The homozygous p.N1060S missense mutation identified in Al-Gazali type multiple epiphyseal dysplasia is a hypomorphic allele whose partial activity is proposed to account for the distinctive skeletal presentation.

evidence.snippet: The phenotype in our patients partially overlaps with the phenotypes associated with those syndromes but they also exhibit some distinctive features including multiple epiphyseal dysplasia

steps/2.description: Deregulated KIF7-dependent Hedgehog/GLI3 signaling disrupts dosed skeletal and craniofacial patterning. The hallmark consequence in Al-Gazali type is multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (abnormal development of the epiphyses of the long bones), accompanied by macrocephaly and a distinctive facial appearance. This skeletal-predominant presentation distinguishes the disorder from the brain- and limb-predominant allelic KIF7 ciliopathies.

evidence.snippet: The early angiogenesis of the retina and its iBRB is a delicate process that is mediated by the canonical Norrin Wnt-signaling pathway in retinal endothelial cells. Pathogenic variants in genes that play key roles within this pathway, such as NDP, FZD4, TSPAN12, and LRP5, have been associated with the incidence of these retinal diseases.
evidence.explanation: Establishes NDP, FZD4, TSPAN12, and LRP5 as components of the shared canonical Norrin-Wnt signaling pathway required for normal retinal vascular development.

evidence.snippet: Interest in norrin signaling within the Wnt/β-catenin pathway arises from its crucial role in maintaining BRB integrity through the activation of the FZD4 receptor and LRP5/6 co-receptors, leading to the stabilization of endothelial junctional complexes and the maintenance and restoration of retinal vascular barrier properties
evidence.explanation: Documents that Norrin-FZD4-LRP5/6 signaling stabilizes retinal endothelial junctional complexes, mechanistically linking pathway loss to blood-retinal barrier breakdown. Evidence source is OTHER because this is a review.

steps/0.description: Loss-of-function NDP variants impair Norrin ligand activity, disrupting Norrin-FZD4-LRP5-TSPAN12 canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling in retinal vascular endothelium. This signaling axis is required for deep retinal vascular plexus formation and stabilization of endothelial junctional complexes that maintain the inner blood-retinal barrier; its loss produces the combined degenerative and proliferative retinal vascular pathology (incomplete vascularization with secondary neovascularization and exudation) seen across the NDP-related retinopathy spectrum.

evidence.snippet: Norrin, secreted by retinal Müller cells, activates canonical Wnt signaling via Frizzled-4 and co-receptors.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the paracrine arrangement this node describes, in which the Muller glial cell is the source and the endothelium the target.

evidence.snippet: Loss-of-function mutations abolish intraretinal capillary formation in mice.
evidence.explanation: States the severity of the developmental failure this node asserts: intraretinal capillary formation is abolished, not merely impaired.

steps/1.description: The retinal consequence of the signalling deficit, and the step at which this disease separates from an ordinary vasculopathy. Norrin is secreted by Muller glia and acts on the endothelium beside them, so the affected cell and the signalling cell are different; the vessels never receive the instruction to grow inward from the superficial plexus and form the deep intraretinal capillary beds. In Ndp-null mice intraretinal capillary formation is abolished outright rather than merely reduced. Severity in humans scales with residual signal, from a peripheral avascular zone in X-linked FEVR to near-total retinal hypovascularization in Norrie disease.

evidence.snippet: We found that cochlear vascular pathology occurs earlier than previously reported and precedes sensorineural hearing loss.
evidence.explanation: Mouse model study demonstrates that cochlear microvascular pathology precedes, and therefore is not a consequence of, the sensorineural hearing loss of Norrie disease.

evidence.snippet: The work defines a disease mechanism whereby early malformation of the cochlear microvasculature precedes loss of vessel integrity and decline of endocochlear potential, leading to hearing loss and hair cell death while sparing spiral ganglion cells.
evidence.explanation: Defines the mechanistic sequence: microvascular malformation, loss of endocochlear potential, then hair cell death, with spiral ganglion cells relatively spared.

steps/2.description: Norrin-Wnt signaling is also required for cochlear vascular development. In Norrie disease, early malformation of the cochlear microvasculature precedes loss of vessel integrity, decline of the endocochlear potential, and subsequent hair cell death, explaining why hearing loss in Norrie disease has a later, progressive onset distinct from the congenital retinal blindness.

evidence.snippet: In humans, mutations in NDP, which encodes norrin, cause Norrie disease, characterized by retinal hypovascularization and congenital blindness, and X-linked familial exudative vitreoretinopathy (FEVR), resembling retinopathy of prematurity (ROP).

steps/3.description: At the severe end of the spectrum the avascular retina is also dysplastic, producing the retrolental fibrovascular mass historically called pseudoglioma, with retinal detachment usually present at or shortly after birth and blindness from infancy. The same lesion at higher residual signal gives X-linked FEVR, whose peripheral avascularity and exudative complications resemble retinopathy of prematurity - a resemblance that is phenotypic convergence on ischaemic retina, not shared aetiology, since ROP begins with hyperoxic vessel arrest rather than with a Norrin lesion.

steps/1.description: LMP1 is the primary EBV oncoprotein in NPC, functioning as a constitutively active receptor that mimics CD40 signaling. LMP1 activates NF-kB, MAPK, and PI3K/AKT pathways, promoting cell survival, proliferation, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition.

evidence.snippet: Network pharmacology analysis identified 27 potential targets of AE acting on NPC, screening out 10 core targets including EGFR, SRC, and STAT3, which are closely associated with tumor signaling.

evidence.snippet: In vitro validation showed that AE significantly suppressed the phosphorylation levels of EGFR, SRC, and STAT3, as well as PD-L1 expression, in NPC C666-1 and CNE1 cells, while reducing cell viability and migration capacity.

steps/2.description: The EGFR/SRC/STAT3 signaling axis is a critical multi-target pathway in NPC oncogenesis, independent of EBV-driven mechanisms. EGFR activation triggers SRC-mediated STAT3 phosphorylation, which drives transcription of downstream oncogenic targets including PD-L1 (promoting immune evasion), as well as genes promoting cell proliferation and migration. This axis represents a therapeutic target validated through network pharmacology, molecular docking, and in vitro experiments in NPC cell lines.

steps/3.description: LMP2A is a viral protein that mimics an activated B cell receptor, providing survival signals that prevent viral lytic reactivation and maintain latency. In epithelial cells, LMP2A activates PI3K/AKT and promotes cell motility.

evidence.snippet: Furthermore, we showed that PD-L1 was associated with worse disease-free survival in NPC patients. These results imply that blocking both the LMP1 oncogenic pathway and PD-1/PD-L1 checkpoints may be a promising therapeutic approach for EBV positive NPC patients.

evidence.snippet: Netherton syndrome (NS) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder caused by SPINK5 mutations, resulting in a deficiency in its processed protein LEKTI.
evidence.explanation: This directly supports SPINK5 as the causal gene and links genotype to LEKTI deficiency.

evidence.snippet: The identification of SPINK5, which encodes for the serine protease inhibitor LEKTI, as the gene responsible for Netherton syndrome, enabled the search for causative mutations in Netherton syndrome patients and families.
evidence.explanation: This supports SPINK5 as the established disease gene and highlights genotype-phenotype analysis in affected families.

evidence.snippet: Among 162 patients, we identified 324 allele variants, comprising 75 different mutations.
evidence.explanation: This supports broad allelic heterogeneity and the need for comprehensive SPINK5 variant interpretation.

evidence.snippet: Genetic analysis revealed that the patient harbored compound heterozygous mutations in the SPINK5 gene, including a missense mutation in exon 26 (c.2475G > T, p.Trp825Cys).
evidence.explanation: This supports ongoing expansion of pathogenic SPINK5 variant classes, including missense alleles.

evidence.snippet: Subsequently, genetic testing identified a defective SPINK5 gene, leading to a diagnosis of NS.
evidence.explanation: This provides additional contemporary clinical evidence of SPINK5 defects as the diagnostic molecular basis of NS.

evidence.snippet: We identified a novel frameshift mutation c.2474_2475del (p.Glu825Glyfs*2) in the SPINK5 gene.
evidence.explanation: This adds evidence that novel SPINK5 pathogenic variants continue to be identified in NS.

genes/0.notes: Biallelic SPINK5 loss-of-function is causative, with variant location associated with phenotype severity in reported cohorts.

evidence.snippet: To date, there are no effective therapy for the management of Netherton Syndrome (NS) Patients use emollients with a limited efficacy on scaling and no efficacy on skin inflammation and pruritus.
evidence.explanation: This trial summary supports current reliance on topical supportive care and its limitations.

treatments/0.description: Emollients and topical anti-inflammatory therapy remain baseline management for scaling and eczematous inflammation, though control is often incomplete.

evidence.snippet: The investigators have used a disabled virus (vector) to carry a functional copy of the SPINK5 gene into skin stem cells.
evidence.explanation: This supports an ex vivo lentiviral SPINK5 gene-correction strategy in NS.

evidence.snippet: In this trial the investigators propose grafting of autologous epidermal sheets generated from genetically modified skin stem cells for the treatment of patients with Netherton Syndrome.
evidence.explanation: This supports autologous epidermal sheet grafting from genetically corrected skin stem cells as the investigational treatment approach.

treatments/1.description: Phase I ex vivo lentiviral gene therapy strategy using autologous epidermal sheets generated from genetically modified skin stem cells to restore LEKTI in Netherton syndrome.

evidence.snippet: This review provides a comprehensive overview of the current clinical landscape and future directions of biologics (e.g., dupilumab, secukinumab, ustekinumab) and small-molecule therapies (e.g., JAK inhibitors such as tofacitinib, baricitinib, and upadacitinib) in the treatment of NS.
evidence.explanation: This supports use of cytokine-targeted and JAK-pathway therapies in severe NS.

evidence.snippet: Though evidence remains limited to case reports and small series, preliminary data suggest that cytokine-targeted interventions-particularly those inhibiting IL-4, IL-13, IL-17, IL-36, and JAK pathways-may offer tangible clinical benefits.
evidence.explanation: This supports potential efficacy while acknowledging current evidence limits.

evidence.snippet: Both patients had swift and enduring enhancement of skin lesions during the follow-up period.
evidence.explanation: This case series adds contemporary human evidence that biologic pathway targeting can improve NS skin disease.

treatments/2.description: Biologics and JAK inhibitors are emerging options in severe disease, targeting IL-4/IL-13, IL-17, IL-36, and JAK pathways.

evidence.snippet: Immunoglobulins (13/15 cases) and biologicals (18/21 cases) showed improvement of the skin.
evidence.explanation: This supports observed skin benefit in aggregated case-based treatment evidence.

evidence.snippet: Under this therapy, his skin status, infectious exacerbations, and quality of life all improved.
evidence.explanation: This provides additional pediatric case-level support for IVIG-centered systemic therapy.

treatments/3.description: Systematic review data indicate skin improvement in many reported cases with immunoglobulins and biologics.

evidence.snippet: KEY CLINICAL MESSAGE: High-dose intravenous immunoglobulin exhibits great potential in the treatment of Netherton syndrome.
evidence.explanation: This explicitly supports IVIG as a promising strategy in pediatric NS.

evidence.snippet: The patient was treated with intravenous immunoglobulin due to frequent infections that required multiple hospital admissions.
evidence.explanation: This supports IVIG use in infection-prone NS with severe recurrent admissions.

treatments/4.description: High-dose IVIG has been used in children with recurrent skin/systemic infections and severe inflammatory skin disease, with reported improvement in skin status and infectious exacerbations.

evidence.snippet: When he was 6 years old, dupilumab was added to reduce skin inflammation and improve skin barrier function before food reintroduction.
evidence.explanation: This supports dupilumab targeting inflammatory and barrier manifestations in pediatric NS.

evidence.explanation: This supports real-world use of dupilumab across pediatric and young-adult NS cases.

evidence.snippet: Since treatment with various antihistamines were not effective, we administered dupilumab and found that it was effective in immediate elimination of pruritus and gradual reduction of the rash.
evidence.explanation: This adds additional case-level evidence for dupilumab benefit on pruritus and inflammatory skin burden.

treatments/5.description: Dupilumab has shown improvement in pruritus and inflammatory skin disease in pediatric and mixed-age NS case reports/series.

evidence.snippet: After 2 injections, the patient's condition markedly improved and the effect after the last injection was maintained for 4-5 months.
evidence.explanation: This supports clinically meaningful short-term and sustained response to secukinumab in refractory NS.

evidence.snippet: The child received treatment with dupilumab, while the 19-year-old woman alternated between using dupilumab and secukinumab.
evidence.explanation: This supports secukinumab use as part of targeted biologic treatment strategies in NS.

treatments/6.description: IL-17A blockade with secukinumab has shown clinical improvement in refractory NS in case-level evidence.

evidence.snippet: Following six months of Abrocitinib therapy, the patient exhibited marked improvement in skin rash and overall disease severity.
evidence.explanation: This supports JAK1 inhibition as a promising targeted option in NS.

treatments/7.description: JAK1 inhibition with abrocitinib has shown symptomatic and severity improvements in case-level NS evidence.

evidence.snippet: In this study, we describe our experience with secukinumab (IL-17A inhibitor) and dupilumab (IL-4/IL-13 inhibitor) treatment of a group of pediatric patients with severe Neterton syndrome.
evidence.explanation: This supports real-world investigational use of combination biologic therapy in severe pediatric NS.

treatments/8.description: Combination IL-17A and IL-4/IL-13 blockade has been reported in severe pediatric NS cohorts.

evidence.snippet: Genetic analysis revealed five different homozygous loss-of-function variants in WBP4.
evidence.explanation: Defines the allelic spectrum underlying the disorder.

evidence.snippet: All variants were absent or had an extremely low frequency (<0.01%) in public databases.
evidence.explanation: Population-database rarity of every reported allele supports pathogenicity of this variant class.

steps/1.description: Five different homozygous loss-of-function alleles have been reported across eight families, comprising frameshift and other truncating variants plus a multi-exon deletion. The index allele is NM_007187.5:c.499delA p.(Thr167fs) (chr13:g.41072793 GA>G, hg38), predicted to introduce a premature stop codon. A second family carries a homozygous deletion of the last three exons of WBP4 within a ~6.2 Mb region of loss of heterozygosity. All alleles are absent or present at extremely low frequency in population databases.

evidence.snippet: Our results show that in both cases the heterozygote parents show half of WBP4 protein amount relative to the WT control and that probands with homozygous WBP4 mutations have total ablation of WBP4 protein
evidence.explanation: Immunoblot of patient-derived fibroblasts directly demonstrates the null protein state and the intermediate carrier level.

evidence.snippet: Immunoblotting on fibroblasts from two affected individuals with different genetic variants demonstrated a complete loss of protein
evidence.explanation: Independent statement in the peer-reviewed report that the protein is completely absent in patient fibroblasts.

steps/2.description: Immunoblotting of primary fibroblasts from two affected individuals carrying different WBP4 alleles showed total ablation of WBP4 protein, while heterozygous parents retained approximately half the wild-type level. WBP4 mRNA was reduced in the frameshift proband, as expected for nonsense-mediated decay, and the transcript in the deletion proband terminated at exon 7 of 10. This is a true null state rather than a hypomorphic or dominant-negative one, and it explains why two distinct alleles converge on a shared molecular consequence.

evidence.snippet: Additional contacts in the C-terminal helicase cassette are required for allosteric inhibition of Brr2 helicase activity.
evidence.explanation: Direct biochemical demonstration that FBP21 (WBP4) allosterically inhibits the Brr2/SNRNP200 helicase; loss of the protein removes this inhibition.

evidence.snippet: Furthermore, the direct interaction between FBP21 and the U4/U6 di-snRNA was found to reduce the pool of unwound U4/U6 di-snRNA.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the second biochemical activity lost in WBP4-null cells: direct U4/U6 di-snRNA binding that restrains duplex unwinding.

evidence.snippet: Thus, inhibition of SNRNP200 plays a crucial role in splice site selection, which positions WBP4 as a key player with a vital role in determining the outcome of splicing.
evidence.explanation: Background statement in the disease-defining paper articulating why loss of SNRNP200 inhibition should alter splice-site selection. Tagged OTHER because it summarizes prior biochemical literature rather than reporting new data of its own.

steps/3.description: WBP4 (FBP21) is a 376-amino-acid protein with a zinc finger motif and two tandem WW domains that is present exclusively in the spliceosomal B complex, acting immediately before catalytic activation. Biochemical and biophysical work on the protein shows that an intrinsically disordered region binds the C-terminal Sec63 unit of the RNA helicase Brr2 (SNRNP200) and allosterically inhibits its helicase activity, and that direct binding of the protein to the U4/U6 di-snRNA reduces the pool of unwound U4/U6. Because SNRNP200-driven U4/U6 unwinding is the irreversible commitment step of the B-to-Bact transition, losing this brake is expected to alter the kinetics of catalytic activation and hence splice-site selection. The node is marked PROVISIONAL because the biochemical inhibition was characterized in reconstituted systems, and de-repression of SNRNP200 has not been measured directly in WBP4-null patient cells. The biochemical evidence is therefore curated as PARTIAL for this disease-state node rather than as direct support.

evidence.snippet: Our analysis identified 5,675 differential splicing events in 2,859 genes in proband F1-II:1 compared to his parents
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the scale of mis-splicing in WBP4-null patient fibroblasts.

evidence.snippet: Comparing proband F2-II:1 to his parents we identified 2,868 differential splicing events in 1,555 genes
evidence.explanation: Replicates the mis-splicing phenotype in a second, unrelated proband carrying a different allele.

evidence.snippet: RNA sequencing analysis uncovered shared abnormal splicing patterns
evidence.explanation: Peer-reviewed statement that the two probands share an abnormal splicing signature.

steps/4.description: RNA sequencing of primary fibroblasts from two unrelated WBP4-null probands versus their heterozygous parents identified 5,675 differential splicing events in 2,859 genes in the first proband and 2,868 events in 1,555 genes in the second. All splicing-event classes were affected - skipped exons, alternative 5' and 3' splice sites, mutually exclusive exons and intron retention - consistent with a general loss of splice-site fidelity rather than a single mis-spliced target. 619 genes were differentially spliced in both probands despite different alleles and different ethnic backgrounds, and principal-component analysis separated each proband from his parents and from healthy WBP4-wild-type children.

evidence.snippet: We found enrichment for abnormalities of the nervous system and musculoskeletal system, suggesting that the overlapping differentially spliced genes are related to the common phenotypes of the probands
evidence.explanation: Directly states the phenotype enrichment of the shared aberrantly spliced gene set, the link between the splicing defect and the clinical picture. No GO nervous-system-development annotation is attached to this node, because the finding is a gene-set enrichment statistic computed on a fibroblast transcriptome, not a measurement of a developmental process.

evidence.snippet: Seven out of the top ten alternatively spliced genes with highest phenotype match, are known autosomal dominant genes.
evidence.explanation: Supports the interpretation that partial mis-splicing of dosage-sensitive dominant neurodevelopmental genes could produce the phenotype.

evidence.snippet: including in genes associated with abnormalities of the nervous system, potentially underlying the phenotypes of the probands
evidence.explanation: The peer-reviewed report frames the link between mis-spliced nervous-system genes and the clinical phenotype as potential, not demonstrated, which is why this node is marked PROVISIONAL.

steps/5.description: Human-phenotype enrichment analysis of the 619 genes aberrantly spliced in both probands returned abnormalities of the nervous system and of the musculoskeletal system, matching the probands' shared clinical features. Aberrantly spliced genes with the strongest phenotype match include NFIX, TRIO, ANKRD11, SZT2, HUWE1, PIGT, SMARCC2, PEX1, QRICH1 and HRAS, together with SMARCA2, HNRNPH1 and TCF4 - all established neurodevelopmental-disease genes. Seven of the top ten are autosomal dominant genes, which the authors interpret as consistent with partial (dosage-like) mis-splicing mimicking a dominant effect. The node is PROVISIONAL because the enrichment is a statistical association computed in fibroblasts, not a demonstration that any individual transcript is functionally deficient in a patient's brain.

steps/7.description: The non-neurological arm: dysmorphic facial features in most affected individuals, and, in a subset, congenital anomalies of the heart, gastrointestinal tract, skeleton and urogenital system. In the most severely affected individual these coalesced into a clinical diagnosis of VACTERL association with anal atresia, atrial septal defect, hypospadias, cryptorchidism and bilateral hydronephrosis. WBP4 is expressed ubiquitously but most highly in skeletal and cardiac muscle, which the authors relate to the musculoskeletal mis-splicing signature and the cardiac anomaly.

evidence.snippet: The clinical presentation of the different affected individuals was highly variable.

treatments/3.description: Autosomal recessive inheritance with a 25% recurrence risk per pregnancy for carrier couples. open_questions/0.rationale: The load-bearing step of this pathograph is unproven. What has been shown is a statistical association: thousands of splicing changes in patient fibroblasts, of which 619 genes are shared between two probands, and a human-phenotype enrichment for nervous-system and musculoskeletal terms. No individual mis-splicing event has been shown to produce a functional protein deficit, no rescue experiment establishes specificity, and the analysis was performed in fibroblasts rather than neural tissue. The authors close the paper by explicitly calling for further functional work. Until this is resolved, the causal edges from mis-splicing to the clinical phenotype are curated as INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES and the downstream nodes as PROVISIONAL.

evidence.snippet: We hypothesis that skin diseases enrichment which is not part of the probands' phenotypes could suggest a difference in gene expression of skin-related genes between the young probands and their adult parents' fibroblasts.
evidence.explanation: The authors' own acknowledgement that part of the fibroblast signal is an artifact of cell type and donor age rather than disease biology, which is the concrete basis for the model-fidelity concern.

evidence.snippet: While, WBP4 is expressed in all tissues it was found to be higher in the skeletal and heart muscles
evidence.explanation: Tissue-expression asymmetry, cited by the authors from an external expression resource, means the fibroblast compartment is not where WBP4 is most abundant, compounding the fidelity concern. open_questions/1.rationale: This is a model-fidelity question rather than an absence of evidence. Robust experimental data do exist, but exclusively from a mesenchymal, skin-derived, postnatal cell type. Alternative splicing is strongly cell-type and developmental-stage specific, so a nervous-system phenotype enrichment derived from fibroblasts is a proxy, not a measurement of the affected tissue. Two concrete signals in the data support treating the mismatch as real rather than theoretical: the differential-expression analysis returned a skin-phenotype enrichment that the authors themselves attribute to comparing young probands against adult parental fibroblasts rather than to disease biology, and WBP4 expression is reported as highest in skeletal and cardiac muscle rather than in fibroblasts or brain. Resolving this requires the same measurements in human neural cells, which is why the proposed experiments in the companion knowledge gap are the route to closure.

evidence.snippet: Individuals F1-II:1 and F2-II:1 presented the two sides of the spectrum, with one displaying a severe phenotype leading to multiple malformations and premature death (F2-II:1) and one only showing much less severe phenotype, with mainly intellectual disability and motor delay.
evidence.explanation: Documents the extremes of the phenotypic spectrum that the question asks about.

evidence.snippet: This is also supported by the fact that both patients were shown to have complete loss of WBP4 protein.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that the severity difference is not explained by residual protein, which is what makes the variability a genuine open question.

open_questions/2.rationale: Allele nature cannot readily explain the spectrum: both the mildest and the most severe probands have complete ablation of WBP4 protein on immunoblot and share 619 differentially spliced genes, yet one has a multiple-malformation lethal course and the other mainly intellectual disability and motor delay. The authors raise two non-exclusive possibilities - the different nature of the underlying lesion (large deletion versus frameshift, potentially affecting neighbouring sequence) and variable expressivity as an intrinsic property of spliceosomopathies, citing the CWC27 precedent. Genetic modifiers and stochastic developmental effects remain untested. This matters clinically because it is the principal barrier to genotype-based prognostication in counseling.
